pk.context: 400 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: It is stable in gastric acid and rapidly absorbed by mouth. About 20% is protein bound, and most of a dose is excreted unchanged in the urine.
clues.substance: Supplied as the trihydrate; the active moiety has a molecular weight of 365.4.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as an oral suspension of 200 or 400 mg per 5 mL; tablets and chewable tablets are also supplied.
clues.safety: No boxed warning; contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction to it. Diarrhea and rash are the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Infections of the ear, nose and throat, genitourinary tract and skin caused by susceptible bacteria.
clues.mechanism: The label describes it only as an antibacterial drug.

tell: A half-life near 1 hour, with about 60% of a dose excreted in urine within 6 to 8 hours, marks this aminopenicillin.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: Peak concentrations occurred approximately 1 hour after the dose.
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The half-life of amoxicillin is 61.3 minutes
evidence.pill: Each 5 mL of reconstituted bubble-gum-flavored suspension
